requirements.title: The build tool shall report its name and semantic version to standard output when invoked with --version, exiting with code 0

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Version exposure
vision.paraphrase: This is a baseline tool-hygiene requirement, not derived from the vision doc — CLAUDE.md declares --version as the CLI's mechanism for exposing its version to an end user.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit a log line at startup containing its name and semantic version at INFO level

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Version stamped at log startup
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the first log line at process startup must name the tool and its version.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit log records at the levels DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR in human-readable prefixed plain-text format written to standard error

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Logging convention
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the four-level, human-readable, stderr-only logging convention for the build tool.

requirements.title: The build tool shall exit with code 0 on success, code 1 on operational failure, and code 2 on invalid invocation

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Exit code convention
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the 0/1/2 exit-code convention so calling scripts and CI can distinguish success, operational failure, and invocation errors.

requirements.title: The build tool shall reject invocation without a --vault argument with exit code 2 and a usage hint

conops.paraphrase: Every operational scenario begins by the author pointing the tool at a specific vault path — the tool has no meaningful behavior without one, so an invocation lacking --vault is an invalid-invocation case the PM persona surfaced as an implicit negative-path requirement.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write primary build output confirmation to standard output and shall write diagnostics, progress, and log output to standard error

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: stdout / stderr discipline
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares stdout carries primary/parseable output while stderr carries diagnostics, progress, and logs.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit user-facing error messages to standard error that name the problem and name the next user action

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Error message standard
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares that user-facing errors must name both the problem and the next user action.

requirements.title: The build tool shall walk every Markdown file under the vault path and parse its YAML frontmatter (title, tags, status, Related, Referenced By) into a node record

vision.paraphrase: The tool must process Markdown wiki content with structured metadata to transform raw vault files into queryable node records, supporting the graph data structure.
Vault content uses git-committed Markdown with frontmatter-driven metadata; the build tool must parse this frontmatter to extract page attributes for the graph.

conops.paraphrase: When the author points the CLI at a local vault path, the tool walks the vault to discover and parse all Markdown files, extracting their frontmatter into node records.

requirements.title: The build tool shall collapse directional Related and Referenced By frontmatter links between two pages into a single undirected edge in graph-data.json

vision.paraphrase: The graph representation collapses directional backlink relationships into undirected edges to simplify the force-directed visualization.

conops.paraphrase: During parsing, the tool synthesizes undirected graph edges from the frontmatter's directional Related and Referenced By relationships.

requirements.title: The build tool shall assign each node a folder/taxonomy value derived from the page's directory path within the vault

vision.paraphrase: Nodes must be grouped and colored by folder taxonomy to visually cluster related content in the graph.
Node color-coding by folder/taxonomy cluster organizes the graph visually to mirror content structure.

conops.paraphrase: The graph renders nodes colored by their folder/taxonomy cluster, which the tool derives from each page's directory path during the build.

requirements.title: The build tool shall skip a Markdown file with missing or malformed frontmatter, emit a WARN log identifying the file, and continue processing the remaining vault

conops.paraphrase: The tool must handle real-world messiness by gracefully skipping malformed files while continuing to process the rest of the vault.

requirements.title: The build tool shall produce zero nodes and zero edges in graph-data.json, without error, when run against a vault directory containing no Markdown files

vision.paraphrase: The 'generic point-at-a-repo tool' goal implies the tool must behave predictably across arbitrary vault states, including the degenerate case of an empty or not-yet-populated vault, without crashing.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write graph-data.json as a single valid JSON document containing top-level nodes and edges arrays

vision.paraphrase: The tool must emit a valid graph-data.json artifact containing nodes and edges that the Next.js page will fetch client-side.
Static graph-data.json is fetched client-side by the Next.js page; it must be valid JSON with nodes and edges arrays.

conops.paraphrase: The tool builds a valid graph-data.json file containing the parsed nodes and synthesized edges.
The build regenerates graph-data.json to include new pages added to the public vault.

requirements.title: The build tool shall compute a precomputed embedding for each vault page's title, body, and tags and write it to vector-index.json alongside the page id

vision.paraphrase: Build-time precomputed embeddings over page content enable real semantic search at query time without dynamic backend calls.
The tool computes build-time embeddings per page and writes a static vector-index.json asset for client-side cosine-similarity ranking.

conops.paraphrase: The tool computes embeddings per page and writes a vector-index.json file alongside graph-data.json.
The rebuild regenerates vector-index.json with embeddings for new pages.

requirements.title: The build tool shall regenerate graph-data.json and vector-index.json fully on every run, with no incremental/partial update

vision.paraphrase: Static derived artifacts (graph-data.json and vector-index.json) are regenerated fully on each build with no incremental updates.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write its output assets only to the local path specified by the user and shall never transmit vault content to any network destination

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary ensures private vault content never leaves the local machine during build.
Content isolation guarantees the tool only outputs to local paths and makes no network calls that could leak private content.

conops.paraphrase: Local iteration against the private second-brain produces output JSON assets only to the local build directory, never published.

requirements.title: The build tool shall require an explicit --vault path argument for every invocation and shall never fall back to a default or previously used vault path

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary requires explicit vault path on every invocation to prevent accidental use of wrong vault.
Input supports local filesystem path only, requiring an explicit --vault argument.

requirements.title: The deployed production build configuration shall reference a single hardcoded --vault path pointing at the dedicated public vault, with no build-time flag or environment variable able to override it

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary requires the production build configuration to hardcode the public vault path with no override capability.

requirements.title: The repository shall never contain a committed file referencing the second-brain private vault's filesystem path

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary prevents accidental exposure by ensuring no committed code references the private vault's path.

requirements.title: The build tool shall include newly added vault pages in graph-data.json and vector-index.json on the next run without any tool-code changes

vision.paraphrase: The tool must be generic, supporting point-at-a-repo operation without code changes as vault content evolves.
Rebuild-on-publish workflow allows new vault pages to appear in the live graph on rebuild without tool modifications.

conops.paraphrase: When new pages are added to the public vault, rebuilding the tool generates updated graph-data.json and vector-index.json automatically.

requirements.title: The build pipeline shall support producing a full Next.js static export that embeds the current graph-data.json and vector-index.json, deployable with no server runtime

vision.paraphrase: Live-feeling static graph requires a Next.js page that fetches graph-data.json client-side and renders via react-force-graph.
Build pipeline produces static assets (graph-data.json and vector-index.json) fetched client-side by the Next.js /graph page.

conops.paraphrase: The Next.js static export build packages the current graph and vector assets for static hosting.
